_comment: Mutation testing for the TypeScript domains (builder/, release/, metrics/). The Python side
keeps mutmut over hooks/ (see pyproject.toml [tool.mutmut]); the two runs are separate CI jobs
named mutation-ts and mutation-py so they execute in PARALLEL rather than serially — that
parallelism is the reason the Python island is worth keeping at all.
The kill-rate gate itself is NOT enforced here. Stryker's own thresholds would report a second,
independently-configured number; instead release/checkMutationGate.mts reads the JSON report
and applies release/mutation-gate.json — the same file the Python gate reads. One threshold,
`mutate` covers builder/, release/ and metrics/, except each domain's own bin/. The bin/ entry
points are logic-free: they resolve a path, call one exported function and exit, so every
mutant in them is either equivalent or unkillable by a unit test. Excluding a logic-free
directory is honest; silencing individual mutants inside real logic is not, and the
`coverageAnalysis: all` rather than perTest — perTest mis-attributed coverage under the Vitest
runner and reported mutants as survived that the suite demonstrably kills.
